segments.text: You are going to listen to a recorded message about a bus tour.
First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.
Now, listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
Thank you for calling the line for Bristol City Bus Tour. This is a recorded message.
In about four minutes, we will provide you what you need to know about the tour.
Being one of the best cities to live in Britain, Bristol has attracted tourists from all over the
world for many years. One of the best ways to get to know the city is to take the bus tour,
which provides a delightful viewing experience from one of our open-top buses. The round-trip
tour of the city includes five stops where passengers can get on and off the bus. The
The first stop is where many people arrive in the city, Bristol Temple Mead's railway
station, the oldest and largest in the city.
While waiting for the bus, visitors can enjoy the historical design of the station.
The next stop is the city's most iconic structure, the Clifton Suspension Bridge.
Along with those beautiful pictures you might take here, adventurous and adrenaline-seeking
tourists can't miss the opportunity for a bungee jump.
However, you need to book in advance to do this.
Passing the bridge, the bus tour continues to carry passengers to the Bristol Zoo.
Here there is a variety of animals, ranging from small bugs to big gorillas, from flying
birds to swimming penguins.
For those who are interested in fancy clothes and big brands, the next stop is for you.
After leaving the zoo, the bus takes you to Cabot Circus, the biggest shopping mall
in the city.
Our advice is to go here in the mornings when it is rather quiet.
It gets busy in the afternoon, especially in the summer.
The last stop is Bristol's Harbourside, where many restaurants and pubs are located.
The Bristol Museum and Art Gallery, which is a few minutes' walk away from the harbour,
is also a great place to spend time in.
Before you listen to the rest of the message, you have some time to look at questions 15-20.
Now, listen carefully and answer questions 15 to 20.
Now some details of the costs and timings.
An adult ticket costs £18, children under 16 £8 and student tickets are £13, but you
must bring your student card.
A family ticket costs £36 and it includes two adults and up to two children.
tickets can be used up to 10 times within 48 hours. This means that you can
get on and off the bus up to a maximum of 10 times within two days. So you could,
for instance, start the tour in the afternoon and finish the tour the day
after, as long as you schedule it in 10 rides. You can purchase tickets at any
of the five stops. You can also book tickets online on our website or over
this phone line, just wait until the end of this message and follow the next steps.
When booking online, you need to print your e-ticket.
Do not show it on your device because the driver cannot stamp on it.
When booking over the phone, you can collect your tickets at any of the stops by simply
giving the staff your reference number.
Buses start running from 9am and the last one leaves the station at 5pm.
There is a 30-minute interval between each bus, and it takes about 60 minutes for a bus
to finish its route.
There are many attractions at each of the stops, so there will be plenty to do wherever
you get off the bus.
The bus tickets do not include entrance fees to any of these attractions, except for the
museum near the harbor side.
If you purchase 10 or more tickets in advance, you can book a local guide who can show
you around and give you all the information needed with no additional fee. We also have
an audio commentary that has been specially recorded for the bus tour by the tourist office.
Headphones are available on the bus and are easy to operate. There is no extra charge for
these, just plug in, select the required language and adjust the volume.
Thank you for calling Bristol City Bus Tour and we look forward to seeing you soon on one of
of our tour buses. This is the end of Section 2. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers
to Section 2. Now, turn to Section 3.
